subject: enhance riscv-v implementation performance.
change_summary: XXH3_accumulate_512_rvv: loop index steps by vl elements, swap mask made static const, acc loaded first, redundant '& 0xffffffff' on data_key>>32 removed (vmul_vv(lo32(data_key), data_key>>32)).

units.name: XXH3_accumulate_512_rvv
units.evidence: Alive2: 'ERROR: Unsupported type: <vscale x 2 x i64>' / 'Unsupported instruction: call <vscale x 2 x i64> @llvm.riscv.vle.nxv2i64.i64(...)' -> 'Could not translate'

units.name: XXH3_64bits_withSeed(p,1024,seed) on riscv64 rv64gcv
units.evidence: Alive2 cannot translate scalable-vector RVV intrinsics (target_api_len1024)

notes: x86-64 IR unchanged: wrapper with all one-shot APIs (XXH32/XXH64/XXH3_64 seed+secret/XXH3_128, symbolic len) compiled with -march=x86-64-v3 and with default SSE2 gives identical modules except !srcloc line metadata (x86_ident_v3/, x86_ident_sse2/); riscv64 -march=rv64gc (no V) also identical target IR (ident_rv64gc_novector/). RVV intrinsics compile to scalable-vector LLVM types (<vscale x N x i64>) and llvm.riscv.* calls, which Alive2 cannot translate at all; even with -march=rv64gcv_zvl512b -mrvv-vector-bits=zvl the IR keeps scalable types (vscale_range(8,8)), see 2973489/compile_rvv_zvl512/. Inputs are value args (U8ARGS) copied into local arrays; XXH3_accumulate_512/XXH3_scrambleAcc/XXH3_initCustomSecret are the library's own dispatch macros. Flags: --target riscv64-linux-gnu, cflags '-O3 -fno-strict-aliasing -fno-vectorize -fno-slp-vectorize -w -nostdlibinc -isystem _work2020/cross_sysinc -march=rv64gcv' + '-DXXH_NO_INLINE_HINTS=1 -mllvm -inline-threshold=100000' (no -ffreestanding so memcpy stays a builtin). Sanity: target_scramble and target_initsecret IR identical old/new (unchanged functions). The removed AND is mathematically redundant (logical >>32 of a u64 is < 2^32) but this is manual reasoning, not a checker result.
